title: A global education platform embeds live student reporting with Metabase.
headline: Advantages School International is an accredited K-12 online private school serving students worldwide.
challenge: Reporting on student progress reached families only at fixed points in the year, by which time any intervention was late.
solution: Embedded per-student dashboards in the parent portal, alongside internal cohort reporting for teaching staff.
results: Families see progress as it happens, and staff identify attendance and assessment drop-off within the week rather than the term.
body:
## Why live reporting

A periodic report summarises something that has already finished. For a student whose engagement slipped weeks ago, it arrives long after a conversation would have helped.

## What changed

Parents see attendance, assessment and submitted work for their own children, strictly scoped. Staff see the same data in aggregate with cohort comparison.

title: Alto uses Metabase for easy and effective company-wide data analysis.
headline: Alto is an investment platform that helps individual investors diversify their portfolios by offering access to alternative assets, traditionally available only to professional investors.
challenge: The existing analytics stack was expensive, slow to work with, and unpopular enough that teams avoided it.
solution: A web-first, container-friendly deployment alongside the existing infrastructure, with dashboards teams could build themselves.
results: Platform cost fell sharply and usage spread well beyond the data team.
body:
## Why they moved

The previous tool required local installation, did not fit the deployment model, and had low satisfaction across the company.

## What the data team does now

Departments manage their own collections. The data team maintains the models underneath rather than fielding requests.

title: AngelList Venture enables everyone on their team to explore data with Metabase.
headline: AngelList Venture brings venture online with private, professional fundraising tools for top quality startups and investors.
challenge: Data access was concentrated in a small group, so most questions arrived as requests rather than being answered directly.
solution: Self-service analytics over modelled data, opened to every team rather than rationed.
results: People across the business explore data directly, and the data team moved from answering questions to maintaining the foundations.
body:
## The bottleneck

When only a few people can query, every question becomes a ticket and the queue defines the team's week.

## What helped

Modelling first. Agreeing definitions before opening access meant self-service produced consistent answers rather than contradictory ones.

title: Aula cuts support tickets by 87% with Metabase Embedded Analytics.
headline: Aula is a digital learning platform designed to make online education more engaging for both educators and students. Over 200,000 students have used Aula so far.
challenge: Customers asked repeatedly for reporting on engagement, and each request arrived as a support ticket.
solution: Embedded analytics inside the learning platform, scoped per institution.
results: Support tickets fell substantially once customers could answer their own questions.
body:
## Support load as a signal

A recurring question in a support queue is usually a missing feature. Reporting requests were the clearest example.

## The approach

One embedded dashboard, filtered per institution, rather than bespoke reports per customer.

title: Axway embedded air-gapped Metabase to give banking clients secure, self-service analytics.
headline: Axway embedded Metabase Enterprise into their accounting software, using air-gapping to deliver white-labeled analytics to heavily regulated, on-premise banking clients—turning the user experience around with out-of-the-box dashboards and self-service exploration.
challenge: Banking clients required analytics inside the product, running in environments with no outbound network access.
solution: White-labelled embedded analytics deployed air-gapped, with dashboards shipped as part of the product.
results: Regulated clients get self-service exploration without the deployment leaving their network.
body:
## Air-gapped by requirement

Regulated environments frequently prohibit outbound connections entirely, which rules out most hosted analytics.

## What shipped

Out-of-the-box dashboards plus the ability for clients to explore, all within their own perimeter.

title: How Metabase helps every team at Bdeo get insights from their data.
headline: Bdeo develops Visual Intelligence technology for the insurance industry, both motor and home insurance, for policy underwriting and claims management processes.
challenge: Each team kept its own view of performance, and the numbers did not reconcile.
solution: Shared models over the core data, with team-specific dashboards built on the same definitions.
results: Teams work from one set of definitions, and cross-team reporting agrees.
body:
## Reconciliation first

The work was less about dashboards than about settling which definition of each metric was correct.

## Afterwards

Teams build their own reporting on top, which is sustainable in a way that a central reporting queue is not.

title: Billing company embeds Metabase in their SaaS platform to give people easy-to-use analytics.
headline: Billing platform transforms the way SaaS companies operate, offering an all-in-one billing and RevOps solution that seamlessly manages billing, quoting, self-service, tenant management, advanced analytics, and revenue recognition with effortless precision.
challenge: Customers wanted analytics on their own billing activity, and building a reporting interface in-house would have taken a quarter.
solution: Embedded dashboards inside the platform, scoped per customer account.
results: Analytics shipped as a product feature without diverting the engineering roadmap.
body:
## Build or embed

Charting is the easy part. The query layer, permissions and caching are where the time goes.

## Scoping

Account identity comes from the signed token, and filtering happens at the data layer rather than in application code.

title: How CaseWhen helped Buena to transform their data analysis with Metabase.
headline: Buena is a modern, digital platform for managing apartments (viewings, payments, maintenance) for both landlords and tenants.
challenge: Property management data was spread across systems with no shared reporting layer.
solution: A consolidated model covering viewings, contracts and maintenance, delivered with an implementation partner.
results: One place to answer operational questions, instead of three systems and a spreadsheet.
body:
## Working with a partner

An external specialist handled the modelling, which is often faster than learning it while building it.

## What it enabled

Operational questions that previously required exporting from two systems now resolve in one view.

title: Cal.com uses Metabase for quick, self-service analytics without relying on engineering.
headline: Cal.com is the open-source Calendly successor that powers scheduling for millions of people around the world.
challenge: Answering product questions required engineering time, so most questions were not asked.
solution: Self-service analytics over product data, available to the whole team.
results: Non-engineers answer their own questions, and engineering time went back to the product.
body:
## The hidden cost

When a question costs an engineer an hour, people stop asking. The lost questions are invisible and are most of the cost.

## After

Support and product query directly. Engineering is involved when the model needs extending, not when someone needs a number.

title: Metabase helps Cetec ERP deliver white-labeled, enterprise-grade BI to manufacturers.
headline: Cetec ERP provides a full suite ERP software for manufacturers and distributors that is practical, intuitive, robust, and flexible to the needs of any manufacturing company.
challenge: Manufacturing customers needed reporting inside the ERP, with each customer seeing only their own operation.
solution: White-labelled embedded analytics with per-tenant data segregation.
results: Enterprise-grade reporting shipped as part of the product rather than as a separate tool.
body:
## Why white-label

Customers should not perceive reporting as a different product. Styling and navigation had to match.

## Isolation

Tenant scoping is enforced at the data layer, which is both safer and easier to demonstrate to a customer's auditor.

title: How Chromatic replaced ad-hoc SQL with shared, self-serve analytics
headline: Chromatic replaced Google Data Studio with Metabase to give the whole company a unified, intuitive workspace for product and business analytics—and is now embedding Metabase for customer-facing insights.
challenge: Reporting relied on ad-hoc SQL written by a few people, so results were inconsistent and hard to share.
solution: Shared, modelled analytics replacing the previous reporting tool, with self-serve exploration for the whole team.
results: Analysis is shared and repeatable rather than re-derived each time someone needs it.
body:
## The problem with ad-hoc

A query in someone's editor is not a shared asset. The next person rewrites it, slightly differently.

## What changed

Saved, named questions that others build on, which turns one person's analysis into something the team owns.

title: Metabase helps every team at Clockwise to get sense of their data.
headline: Clockwise optimizes your team’s calendars to create more time in everyone’s day. It brings together a powerful optimization engine with a personal calendar assistant to make your work life run smoothly.
challenge: Teams needed answers from product data but depended on a small group to get them.
solution: Self-service analytics over modelled product events.
results: Every team queries directly, and the data team supports the model rather than the queue.
body:
## Scaling access

The constraint was never the data. It was how many people were able to ask it anything.

## The model layer

A well-named model covering core events removed most of the need for joins, which is what had been blocking non-specialists.

title: Cypress uses Metabase for data-driven decision-making.
headline: Cypress is an end-to-end testing framework used for testing anything that runs in the browser. Written in Javascript, Cypress is used by hundreds of thousands of developers and QA engineers globally to write, run, and debug automated tests for web applications.
challenge: Decisions were being made without easy access to the data that should have informed them.
solution: Dashboards over product and usage data, accessible across the company.
results: Routine decisions now start from a number rather than a recollection.
body:
## Access changes behaviour

The measurable change was not better analysis. It was that people checked at all.

## Keeping it trustworthy

Ownership on each dashboard, so there is a person to ask when a number looks wrong.

title: Dribbble uses Metabase to democratize data across all their teams.
headline: Dribbble is the world’s leading community for creatives to share, grow, and get hired.
challenge: Data was available in principle and reachable by very few people in practice.
solution: Company-wide self-service analytics over shared models.
results: Teams across the business explore data directly rather than requesting extracts.
body:
## Democratising access

The gap between having data and being able to use it is mostly tooling and permissions, not analytical skill.

## What made it work

Modelling the data so common questions did not require understanding the schema.

title: Fabulous builds an efficient system of business reporting within the company with Metabase.
headline: Fabulous is a mobile app helping thousands of people every day to change their lifestyles by integrating healthy habits into their lives. Fabulous is ranked 5th Health & Fitness App and has over 30 million users.
challenge: Business reporting was assembled manually and inconsistently between weeks.
solution: Automated reporting over shared models, with dashboards owned by the teams that use them.
results: Reporting happens on schedule and does not depend on one person being available.
body:
## Key-person risk

Several important numbers existed because one person remembered to update something. That is a reporting system in name only.

## Now

Scheduled, owned, and the same every week.

title: How Faros.ai embeds Metabase into their multi-tenant SaaS product.
headline: Faros AI is an engineering operations platform that brings all engineering data in one place to give engineering leaders a single-pane view of their entire software development lifecycle.
challenge: Customers needed engineering operations reporting inside the product, across many tenants.
solution: Embedded multi-tenant dashboards with isolation enforced at the data layer.
results: Reporting became a product capability rather than a series of bespoke requests.
body:
## Multi-tenant from the start

Designing for one customer and generalising later is how per-customer dashboards accumulate.

## Verification

Cross-tenant isolation is asserted in automated tests, because that failure is silent when it happens.

title: Metabase helps Floryn simplify their BI, reduce costs, and empower teams to explore data easily.
headline: Floryn provides SMEs with fast, digital, data-driven business loans and working capital. They’ve financed over €330M in credits to SMBs in the Netherlands.
challenge: The existing BI setup was costly and difficult for non-specialists to use.
solution: A simpler analytics layer over the existing data, opened to every team.
results: Costs fell and more people are able to explore data without assistance.
body:
## Simplification as the goal

The previous tool was capable and nobody outside the data team could use it. Capability nobody can reach is not capability.

## Lending data

Loan book and risk reporting are now maintained by the teams that depend on them.

title: Gojek brings company-wide transparency to customer care with Metabase.
headline: Gojek is a leading on-demand service provider. As of June 2020, Gojek has about 170 million users throughout Southeast Asia.
challenge: Customer care operated at a scale where reporting had to be both company-wide and granular.
solution: Shared analytics across customer care, with embedded views for operational teams.
results: Transparency across a large operation, with teams able to drill into their own area.
body:
## Scale changes the problem

At this size, one dashboard cannot serve everyone. The model has to support many views over consistent definitions.

## Consistency

Shared definitions were the prerequisite. Without them, every team's view disagrees with every other.

title: Griffin Marine Services uses Metabase's built-in CSV database for reporting.
headline: Griffin Marine Services provides engineering, maintenance, and project management for the commercial and defense marine industry. Their clients include the Royal Australian Navy (RAN) and Australian Border Force (ABF).
challenge: Operational data lived in spreadsheets with no database behind it.
solution: Uploading CSV data directly into the analytics layer, with reporting built on top.
results: Reporting without a warehouse or a pipeline, which suited the size of the operation.
body:
## Not every team needs a warehouse

For a team of this size, a pipeline would have been more machinery than the problem required.

## What they use

Direct CSV upload, modelled lightly, reported on consistently.

title: Hola Health replaces manual reporting with real-time operational visibility in under three months.
headline: Hola Health is an Australia-based telehealth provider operating in Australia and the UK. They use Metabase to standardize metrics, automate reporting, and support fast operational decisions.
challenge: Operational reporting was manual, so visibility lagged behind what was happening in the service.
solution: Dashboards over appointment and clinician data, replacing the manual process.
results: Real-time operational visibility, established quickly.
body:
## Latency was the issue

The reporting was accurate and arrived too late to act on, which is a familiar failure in operational settings.

## What shipped

Live views of appointments, utilisation and wait times, owned by the operations team.

title: Hurb uses Metabase to improve their decision-making process and increase earnings.
headline: Hurb is a leading online travel platform based in Latin America that has over 25 million registered travelers all over the world.
challenge: Decision-making relied on reports that took time to produce and were not always current.
solution: Self-service dashboards over booking and customer data.
results: Faster decisions, with teams able to check rather than request.
body:
## Travel data moves quickly

In a business where pricing and demand shift daily, a weekly report is a historical document.

## The change

Teams look at current numbers themselves, and the reporting function supports the model rather than producing documents.

title: Insocial saves 1,100+ engineering hours with Metabase
headline: Insocial helps organizations understand what their customers and employees think.
challenge: Generating customer-facing feedback dashboards required engineering effort for each new client.
solution: Embedded dashboards generated from a shared template, scoped per client.
results: A large amount of recurring engineering effort removed.
body:
## Per-client work does not scale

Every bespoke dashboard is a maintenance commitment that compounds with each new customer.

## The alternative

One dashboard, parameterised. New clients require configuration rather than engineering.

title: How KLog uses Metabase to deliver shipping reports to their clients.
headline: KLog provides freight-forwarding services and a digital platform for international commerce administration. KLog.co is a bootstrapped business, and they’ve already served over 3,000 clients to yield $100M in Revenue.
challenge: Freight customers wanted shipment reporting, and operations produced it by hand.
solution: Embedded dashboards in the customer portal covering shipment status and exceptions.
results: Customers self-serve, and the manual reporting run was retired.
body:
## The weekly run

Manually assembled customer reports are stale on arrival and consume operational capacity every week.

## What customers get

Status and exceptions as they happen, which turned out to matter more than the hours saved.

title: Kula and Standard Co team up to empower female entrepreneurs with Metabase.
headline: Kula Project is a nonprofit aiming to eradicate poverty by developing women entrepreneurs in Rwanda.
challenge: Programme outcomes needed reporting to funders, with limited capacity to produce it.
solution: Shared models over programme data, with dashboards per reporting requirement.
results: Funder reporting is produced on schedule without consuming programme capacity.
body:
## Capacity is the constraint

For a small organisation, every hour on compliance reporting is an hour not spent on the programme.

## Working with a partner

An implementation partner handled setup, which is often the difference between a project happening and not.

title: Lime Technologies white-labels Metabase to provide their customers with answers about their business.
headline: Lime Technologies is a Customer Relationship Management supplier with offices in the Nordics, Netherlands, and Germany that delivers what they call “CRM with a twist” to make sure their clients exceed their customers’ expectations.
challenge: CRM customers wanted analytics on their own data, branded as part of the product.
solution: White-labelled embedded analytics within the CRM.
results: Customers answer their own questions inside the product they already use.
body:
## Branding matters

Analytics that looks like a different product undermines the impression that it is part of the one you sold.

## Scope

Each customer sees only their own data, enforced below the application layer.

title: Metabase expert CaseWhen helps Linstol become more data-driven.
headline: Linstol, the largest supplier of headphones/earbuds in the world (bigger than Samsung), embeds Metabase in their web portal to stay on top of their inventories.
challenge: Reporting across a distribution business was fragmented and slow to produce.
solution: Consolidated analytics over sales and inventory data, delivered with a partner.
results: A single view of the business, maintained by the teams that use it.
body:
## Consolidation

The difficulty was less technical than definitional: agreeing what a sale, a return and a unit meant across regions.

## Outcome

One model, several team-specific views built on it.

title: How Marketfuel got to proof of concept on their in-app reporting in under 30 days
headline: Marketfuel is an all-in-one eCommerce platform designed for promotional marketing agencies to create their own online store within a single afternoon. The platform enables agencies to manage inventory, order fulfillment, label printing, and more through a single application.
challenge: In-app reporting was a customer requirement, and a from-scratch build would have delayed the roadmap.
solution: Embedded analytics against existing data, with no new pipeline.
results: A working proof of concept very quickly, which de-risked the decision.
body:
## Proof of concept first

The value of getting to a prototype quickly is that it converts an architectural argument into something people can look at.

## What followed

The prototype became the shipped feature with styling and scoping work, not a rewrite.

title: Matter saves 30% of their growth budget, making data-informed decisions with Metabase.
headline: Matter is a free Slack app that helps teams to recognize each other with Kudos, rewards, and continuous feedback – all inside Feedback Friday.
challenge: Growth spending decisions were made without clear visibility of which channels produced lasting users.
solution: Analytics joining acquisition data to product engagement.
results: A meaningful share of growth budget redirected away from channels that were not working.
body:
## Volume is not quality

Channels with identical cost per signup can have completely different activation rates, and spend reports hide that entirely.

## The join

Connecting acquisition source to downstream engagement is the whole exercise.

title: Metabase helps myAgro enable true self-service analytics.
headline: myAgro is a non-profit agritech social enterprise based in West Africa. myAgro has developed a mobile savings model that allows farmers to invest their own funds in high-quality seed, fertilizer, and agricultural training to increase their harvest and income by 50-100%.
challenge: Field programme data needed to be usable by teams without analytical training.
solution: Modelled data with dashboards designed for non-specialists.
results: Field and programme teams answer their own questions.
body:
## Designing for the reader

When the audience has no analytical background, the modelling has to do more work so the interface can do less.

## What that meant

Fewer tables, clearer names, and defaults that are correct without configuration.

title: N26 promotes data literacy in Europe's first mobile bank with Metabase.
headline: N26 is Europe’s first mobile bank, headquartered in Berlin. N26 helps clients manage their bank account on the go, track their expenses, and set aside money in real time.
challenge: A fast-growing bank needed analytics accessible beyond the data team while meeting regulatory expectations.
solution: Governed self-service analytics with permissions mapped to existing groups.
results: Wider access without loosening controls.
body:
## Governance and access together

In a regulated setting these are usually traded against each other. They do not have to be, if permissions are modelled rather than managed by hand.

## Groups, not individuals

Mapping to existing identity groups keeps access correct as people move teams.

title: With Metabase, Onecom delivers real-time, embedded analytics to thousands of customers - without relying on engineering.
headline: Onecom is a managed service provider delivering telecoms, cloud, and data services to enterprise customers across the UK. They offer an integrated customer portal where users can access everything from billing to performance metrics. To support that experience, Onecom needed a reliable, flexible…
challenge: Reporting was needed both internally and for managed-service customers.
solution: Internal dashboards plus embedded customer-facing reporting from the same models.
results: One model serving two audiences, rather than two parallel reporting stacks.
body:
## Shared foundations

Internal and customer-facing reporting usually diverge into separate systems. Building both on one model avoids the divergence.

## The constraint

Customer-facing views need stricter scoping, which is a permissions problem rather than a modelling one.

title: Onepark cut ad hoc requests for data in half after picking up Metabase.
headline: Onepark is a leading European online carpark booking platform, headquartered in Paris.
challenge: Booking and operational data was not easily accessible to the teams who needed it.
solution: Self-service dashboards over booking data.
results: Operational teams track performance without requesting reports.
body:
## Removing the request step

Most operational questions are simple and frequent, which is exactly the category that should never require a ticket.

## Afterwards

The analytics function works on the model rather than on requests.

title: How Owlery cut time iterating on Embedded Analytics from 2 Days of engineering to 2 hours in CS
headline: Founded in 2021, Owlery helps manufacturers and brands optimize their supply chain operations. Their platform integrates with customers' supply chain partners and ERPs to create cohesive workflows that save time, reduce costs, and increase efficiency.
challenge: Manufacturers and brands needed visibility into their own logistics data inside the platform.
solution: Embedded reporting scoped per customer.
results: Customers see their own operation without an export or a request.
body:
## Why embedded

Logistics customers check frequently and briefly. A monthly export does not fit that pattern.

## Scoping

Account identity travels with the session, and filtering happens below the application.

title: Recruit CRM embeds Metabase to offer customers self-serve dashboards inside their app.
headline: Recruit CRM is an AI-Powered, top-rated ATS + CRM for recruitment agencies worldwide
challenge: Recruitment agencies using the product wanted reporting on their own pipelines.
solution: Embedded dashboards inside the applicant tracking product.
results: Reporting became part of the product rather than a request queue.
body:
## Customer-facing from the start

Agencies compare their own performance over time, which requires history and consistency more than it requires flexibility.

## Implementation

One parameterised dashboard rather than per-agency builds.

title: How Metabase became the single source of truth for the Reforge team.
headline: Reforge helps people do the best work of their careers. They offer educational programs, networking opportunities, events, and community to help people understand which strategies have worked for the best companies in the world. All programs are led by actual growth practitioners from leading…
challenge: Understanding how learners engaged with programmes required data the team could not easily reach.
solution: Self-service analytics over programme and engagement data.
results: Programme decisions are informed by engagement data rather than assumption.
body:
## Engagement over completion

Completion rates are easy and misleading. Engagement patterns during a programme are the more useful signal.

## Access

Programme staff query directly rather than requesting analysis.

title: Retargetly builds a data culture with Metabase.
headline: Retargetly is a leading Data Platform company in Latin America that helps brands, agencies, and publishers  create better advertising experiences for consumers through data and technology.
challenge: A data platform business needed internal analytics that could keep up with its own data volume.
solution: Analytics over the existing warehouse with modelled, reusable definitions.
results: Internal teams work from consistent definitions at scale.
body:
## Practising what you sell

Data companies are not automatically good at their own internal analytics, and often worse because everything looks solvable.

## What helped

Treating internal definitions with the same rigour as customer-facing ones.

title: How Sincera uses Metabase embedding to provide their customers with digital advertising and media insights.
headline: Sincera is a modern verification service that helps companies accelerate their competitive velocity. It provides data and infrastructure to answer novel questions in media and advertising with hard, accurate data.
challenge: Customers needed access to verification data in a form they could explore themselves.
solution: Embedded analytics over the verification dataset, scoped per customer.
results: Customers investigate their own data instead of requesting extracts.
body:
## Exploration, not reports

When customers' questions are open-ended, a fixed report generates follow-up requests indefinitely.

## The approach

Give them the ability to filter and drill within their own scope.

title: Spocket saves over 60 hours per month and avoids ad-hoc requests of their data team.
headline: Spocket is the largest online dropshipping marketplace that connects over 80,000 retailers with millions of fast-shipping suppliers around the globe.
challenge: A marketplace connecting two sides needed reporting that reflected both.
solution: Shared models covering supplier and retailer activity, with dashboards per team.
results: Teams see both sides of the marketplace from consistent definitions.
body:
## Two-sided reporting

Marketplace metrics are easy to state and hard to define: an active supplier and an active retailer are different things measured differently.

## Definitions

Settling those was the bulk of the work and the bulk of the value.

title: Sunglass Fix explores their business with Metabase.
headline: Sunglass Fix is a family-owned, premium sunglass lens replacement service, selling brand new ultra High Definition lenses worldwide since 2008.
challenge: A small team needed reporting without the overhead of a data function.
solution: Lightweight analytics over existing order data.
results: Reporting proportionate to the size of the business.
body:
## Right-sizing

Small businesses are frequently sold infrastructure designed for much larger ones.

## What this looks like

A handful of dashboards over the operational database, maintained by the people who use them.

title: Synctera uses Metabase to improve customer satisfaction and self-service analytics.
headline: Synctera is a banking and payments platform that helps companies of all sizes build and scale financial products.
challenge: Banking platform customers required analytics with strict separation between them.
solution: Embedded analytics with per-tenant isolation and curated, vetted content.
results: Customers explore their own data within boundaries that satisfy compliance review.
body:
## Marking what is trustworthy

Distinguishing vetted content from exploratory work tells people where to start, which matters more as the volume grows.

## Isolation

Enforced at the data layer and demonstrable, which is what a compliance review actually asks for.

title: Treebo Hotels makes metrics and KPIs a part of their daily routine with Metabase.
headline: Treebo Hotels is an Indian budget hotel chain that operates on franchising. As of January 2020, Treebo Hotel has over 600 hotels in 113 cities in India.
challenge: A franchise hotel operation needed consistent reporting across independently run properties.
solution: Shared models with per-property dashboards.
results: Properties and head office work from the same definitions.
body:
## Franchise reporting

The difficulty is that each property operates independently but has to be comparable.

## Shared definitions

Occupancy and revenue per room defined once centrally, reported per property.

title: Uptime keeps elevators moving with Metabase.
headline: Uptime helps elevator service providers keep their lifts running. They develop an operation management platform and a predictive maintenance technology that makes it easy to maintain elevators.
challenge: Service providers needed visibility into equipment status across many installations.
solution: Analytics over device and service data, with reporting for service teams.
results: Issues are visible earlier, which shortens response time.
body:
## Connected equipment

Device telemetry is high volume and mostly uninteresting. The value is in surfacing the small fraction that is not.

## What is reported

Status, exceptions and service history, aggregated to the level a service team can act on.

title: Usabilla unlocks analytics for everybody with Metabase.
headline: Usabilla is a user feedback solution for collecting qualitative and quantitative user feedback across digital channels including websites, apps, and emails.
challenge: Feedback data was collected at volume but was hard to analyse across customers and time.
solution: Modelled analytics over qualitative and quantitative feedback.
results: Trends are visible across the dataset rather than per response.
body:
## Qualitative at scale

Individual feedback is readable; thousands of responses need categorisation before any of it is analysable.

## The modelling

Categorising by underlying theme rather than by the form field the respondent selected.

title: Metabase helps Yellow Card scale self-serve analytics across a 200+ person fintech team.
headline: Yellow Card is the largest and first licensed Stablecoin payments orchestrator, empowering businesses across emerging markets with international payments, treasury management, and USD liquidity
challenge: A rapidly growing fintech needed analytics accessible across a large, distributed team.
solution: Self-serve analytics over governed models, with permissions mapped to existing groups.
results: Analytics scaled across the organisation without a corresponding increase in the data team.
body:
## Scaling access, not headcount

The alternative to self-service is hiring analysts in proportion to questions, which does not work.

## Governance

Curated models and clear ownership, so wider access did not mean inconsistent answers.
